notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.309 Arm S: across two invocations, a project hook sleeping 300 ms and a relay hook 0 ms ran concurrently in 24/24 event pairs; the relay started first in 5/12 pairs in invocation 1 and 1/12 in invocation 2. notes.degraded_path_hazard: Arm D on 2.1.309 used a command-specific Bash deny rule and needed two invocations: 5 of 10 runs verified an errored Bash tool result, and every completed run - verified or not - exited 0 and fired exactly one Stop. The 5 unverified runs ended with the model declining the call ('Bash tool isn't available in this session'), the same declined-attempt/deferred-tools shape as the prior pin; it changes probe scenario coverage, not the Stop contract. The historical 2.1.270 extra-Stop hazard did not reproduce. The poller keeps first-payload tolerance for degraded runs.
